what_it_does.name: improve-codebase-architecture
what_it_does.summary: Instructions for an architecture review of a codebase in a fixed vocabulary of module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality. It scopes the scan to a direction the user names or to hot spots in the commit history, has a sub-agent walk the code, and writes deepening candidates with before and after diagrams to a self-contained HTML report in the OS temp directory. Once the user picks a candidate, it grills the decision tree with them and keeps GLOSSARY.md and ADRs current. The user invokes it, the model does not.
tasks: find hot spots in the commit history
find shallow modules and seams that leak
render deepening candidates as an HTML report with before and after diagrams
grill the decision tree of the candidate the user picks
add terms to GLOSSARY.md and offer ADRs for rejected candidates

outputs.what: architecture review with one card per deepening candidate, a recommendation strength badge and a top recommendation
the absolute path of the report and the question which candidate to explore
a record of a rejected candidate with its reason

what_it_does.sample_output: Which of these would you like to explore?

risks.risk: Instructions planted in source files, commit messages, GLOSSARY.md or ADRs reach the agent, since the codebase is read without delimiters or sanitisation.
risks.mitigation: none in the files, C2 notes that boundary markers and sanitisation are absent

risks.risk: Script from cdn.tailwindcss.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net runs in the browser when the report opens, so a changed or compromised CDN file controls the page.
With Mermaid securityLevel loose, file names or comments from the codebase copied into a diagram can run as script in the report.
On a shared machine, the report on the codebase's architecture lands in /tmp, where other users may be able to read it.
GLOSSARY.md in the project is changed inline as decisions crystallize, with no confirmation step stated.

known_problems.problem: Mermaid's layout fights the diagram, or cannot give a deep module the right weight
known_problems.workaround: draw modules as divs with inline SVG arrows positioned over a relative container
